# Workflows

| Workflow | Runs on | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`ci.yml`](ci.yml) | Push to `main` and pull requests | **Palette and contrast** runs `npm run check`, which measures every colour against the contrast floors, tests the paired tokens under simulated colour vision deficiencies and parses every generated file, then `npm run verify`, which rebuilds every file from the palette and fails if anything committed differs. **VS Code package** packages the extension with `@vscode/vsce` and uploads the `.vsix`. **JetBrains plugin** builds the plugin with `./gradlew buildPlugin` on Java 21 and uploads the zip. **Eclipse update site** builds the Eclipse plugin and its p2 update site with Maven and Tycho and uploads the site |
| [`release.yml`](release.yml) | A tag starting with `v`, such as `v0.1.0` | Runs the checks, confirms the tag matches the palette version and the changelog has a section for it, builds the `.vsix`, the JetBrains zip and the Obsidian, Sublime Text, Helix, Emacs and Xcode zips and uploads them as the `zacess-themes-<version>` artifact. The JetBrains plugin build takes this version's changelog section as its Marketplace change notes. Runs in the `release` environment. Publishes to the VS Code Marketplace through a Microsoft Entra identity and to Open VSX through trusted publishing, both with no stored token. Publishes to the JetBrains Marketplace only when the `JETBRAINS_TOKEN` secret exists, otherwise that step is skipped with a line in the run summary. Last, it sends a `themes-release` repository dispatch naming the tag to zacesshq/website, whose deploy workflow rebuilds zacess.com from the new palette. That needs the `SITE_DISPATCH_TOKEN` secret, a fine-grained token limited to that repository with Contents read and write. Without it the step is skipped with a line in the run summary. A failed dispatch is only reported, so the release still succeeds; the website also deploys any new release daily. It never writes to a repository: the GitHub release and the read-only Obsidian and Neovim copies are made afterwards by `scripts/release.mjs` on a maintainer's machine, as described in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#releasing) |
| [`eclipse-site.yml`](eclipse-site.yml) | A tag starting with `v`, also run by hand | Builds the Eclipse plugin, feature and p2 update site with Maven and Tycho on Java 21 and publishes the site to GitHub Pages, where Eclipse installs it from https://zacesshq.github.io/themes/eclipse/. Each run replaces the whole site, so it always holds the version that was built |
| [`marketplace-identity.yml`](marketplace-identity.yml) | Run by hand | Signs in as the Microsoft Entra identity the release uses, prints its Azure DevOps profile id and checks it can publish to the `zacess` publisher on the VS Code Marketplace. Publishes nothing |
| [`markdownlint.yml`](markdownlint.yml) | Push to `main` and pull requests, also run by hand | Lints every markdown file with the rules in `.markdownlint.json` |

Every action is pinned to a full commit SHA with its version in a comment. Dependabot proposes updates
weekly.
